html:
ForgeMCP active development plan

The authoritative source location is [local path]. The original roadmap remains the historical vision; this plan governs completion evidence for ongoing development.

Current coordinated release candidate — October 20, 2026

Current local versions are core 0.3.14, Unreal plugin 0.2.14-alpha.3, and Blender add-on 0.2.36-alpha.1. The exact artifact hashes, acceptance evidence, and limitations are recorded in the coordinated release record [not indexed]. The core suite passes 469 tests; Blender clean-profile acceptance passes; and the packaged Unreal plugin passes a bounded disposable isolated Landscape test. The full UAT BuildPlugin pipeline remains blocked by the installed engine's missing BuildSettings.precompiled manifest. No existing Editor was updated.

Next safe work is a separately authorized deployment to a disposable or preserved isolated project, followed by a controlled World Partition/Landscape test. The observer's unresolved dirty /Script/SlateCore row must remain a review blocker. Do not install into the current long-running Editor or advance Phase 6C from the disposable smoke result; Phase 6C remains NO-GO.

Next Unreal milestone — Splines, PCG and city reconstruction

Prioritize the Splines/PCG implementation specification requested October 16, 2026. Deliver versioned capability inventory and read-only inspection first, followed by spline authoring, roads/junctions/Landscape integration, PCG graph authoring and generation, city districts, and calibrated reference-image reconstruction. Full exposure remains the target; each increment must state its coverage gaps. Reference calibration and accuracy constraints must inform the data contracts from the first increment. The specification records the live baseline, acceptance gates and 1:1-scale accuracy contract; these capabilities are not yet implemented. Existing roadmap obligations and release gates remain active.

Component versions advance when that component receives a validated change. The versions above are the current local release candidates; component versions remain independent and do not imply that every feature or workflow is complete. The coordinated v1.0.0 release is reserved for completion of the roadmap's clean installation, live-session, capability, recovery, and package acceptance criteria.

October 16 engine-wide alpha: UE 5.6.1 Win64 installation and fresh-project native and real stdio MCP inspection passed. Keep the installed alpha snapshot separate from active source development. See acceptance evidence [not indexed] for the 335-test result, full editor-target build, loaded DLL proof and remaining visible UI/performance gates; alpha setup covers updates and rollback.

Alpha.9 brings a reference-inspired React UI into the Unreal editor tab. Its first split-file bundle failed to load from the local file URL; the corrected self-contained bundle passed Chromium runtime and clean-project UE package checks. Rendering and control interaction inside the user's standard desktop Editor remain unverified. See alpha.9 UI acceptance and the white-tab fix record. The transfer actions also use locally embedded official Unreal Engine and Blender marks; see the logo integration record. The reference-matched compact panel is recorded in the layout refinement note.

Objective

Alpha.4 transfer-name retention: Blender-to-Unreal defaults to /Game/Content/Returns/ and uses the exact Blender source object name. The reverse handoff keeps the Unreal asset name as Blender's object name when the optional override is blank. Exact-name collisions are reported instead of silently renamed. See alpha.4 acceptance.

Alpha.3 transfer UX: Import from Blender reports the existing Unreal destination and offers the safe next step; Send to Blender keeps the source name when its optional name override is blank. The engine package was installed and loaded in a fresh project; visible panel acceptance remains. See the fix record.

Alpha.2 transfer fix: built-in /Engine meshes support read-only Send to Blender; typed validation errors no longer disappear inside async exception groups. Both FBX and OBJ panel-worker handoffs and the installed engine copy passed acceptance. Native source stays in the engine installation; use explicit source arguments for host generation and packaging. See the fix record.

October 13 Blender expansion: the source now exposes native operator/RNA catalogs and reviewed creative workflows for primitives, cameras/lights, properties, shader graphs, numeric keys, modifiers/constraints, save-copy and asynchronous PNG renders. The complete source registry contains 104 MCP tools. Native and real stdio MCP tests rendered 4096 × 2304 outputs in disposable sessions. Existing interactive Blender/client processes require their own version refresh. See Documentation/Blender_Creative_Automation.md for exact execution coverage, remaining adapters and acceptance evidence; discovery does not imply universal operator execution.

Develop ForgeMCP into a dependable local MCP platform for practical game-development workflows across Unreal Engine and Blender. Build on the existing server, Unreal plugin, and Blender add-on so an authorized AI client can inspect application state, propose changes, execute supported native operations, verify results, and recover from failures.

Deliver complete workflows for scene and asset creation, Blueprint authoring, materials, rigs and animation, and validated Blender-to-Unreal asset transfer. Each workflow must identify its target session, expose operation limits, protect existing work, report application-level errors, and provide evidence of resulting changes.

Completion requires repeatable installation on a clean environment, reliable use in interactive application sessions, tested failure and recovery behavior, documented capability coverage, and installable packages for both applications. The existence of a tool, a passing unit test, or an adapter health response alone does not prove a complete workflow.

Current capability note — Blender modifiers

The native modifier slice currently supports inspection and reviewed creation of Subdivision, Bevel, Solidify and Weighted Normal modifiers through the existing preview/apply scene recipe. It validates bounded settings, protects linked and edit-mode meshes, includes modifier state in stale-preview checks and rolls back modifiers created by a failed batch. Editing/removing existing modifiers and arbitrary Geometry Nodes graphs remain outside this slice. See Documentation/Development_Status.md for the latest MCP acceptance evidence.

Unreal DataTables now support bounded, read-only schema inspection, paginated row names and exact row-value inspection through three MCP tools. Only /Game and /JasperPrism asset paths are accepted; nested/container values are omitted. The disposable UE 5.6.1 MCP acceptance and unchanged-package hash are recorded in the development status report.

DataAsset support includes native Asset Registry search under /Game or /JasperPrism, loaded UDataAsset subclass discovery, and bounded reflected class schema inspection. The schema reports inherited/editable flags, native property types, container element/key/value types, and reference constraints without loading instances. DataAsset creation now uses a separate reviewed preview/apply path for one new asset of an exact loaded concrete class, with bounded editable initial values and optional explicit saving. Existing-instance editing now uses unreal_preview_data_asset_edit and unreal_apply_data_asset_edit: each operation is bounded to 1–32 supported simple editable reflected properties on one existing asset, requires an exact single-use preview confirmation, rejects stale/dirty targets, and only saves when explicitly requested. Apply preserves a verified pre-edit package backup under the disposable project Saved directory and validates values after save. Native boolean accessors handle Unreal bitfield booleans. Arrays, nested containers, object/asset references, and arbitrary property editing remain unsupported. A disposable UE 5.6.1 test also reopened the saved asset in a fresh Editor process and confirmed the values.

Unreal also exposes unreal_inspect_actor_components for bounded native component hierarchy, attachment, transform, mobility and assigned static-mesh inspection, plus unreal_inspect_component_properties for a bounded set of simple reflected values and editability metadata on one exact loaded component. Neither component tooling provides recursive object/container access. Component values can also be edited through reviewed unreal_preview_component_property_edit / unreal_apply_component_property_edit transactions, with separate level saving. Bitfield booleans use Unreal's native boolean property accessors and verified lowercase read-back; component property reflection class is returned alongside the C++ type string. See the development status record for native MCP acceptance evidence.

Next milestone: validated Blender-to-Unreal asset workflow

October 11–12 live integration checkpoint: the Codex host reports server 0.3.1 and connected Unreal bridge 0.2.8 in ForgeMCPDev. The separate Blueprint showcase passed guarded creation, compilation, save, opening and native read-back. The full ForgeMCPDevEditor target passed after orderly Editor closure; saved Blueprint read-back passed again after restart. See Unreal_MCP_Showcase.md. Other operation families and JasperPrismDev keep their own acceptance gates.

Create or modify a supported asset in Blender, validate and export it, import it into Unreal, place it in a level, and verify scale, orientation, materials, and asset references. Include explicit previews, overwrite protection, recoverable backups, and a structured report for every step. Validate in separate test projects and in interactive Blender and Unreal sessions.

The primary Blender-to-Unreal transfer and return-to-Unreal path handles static meshes using binary FBX. Unreal-to-Blender additionally supports a constrained OBJ route, now covered by an asymmetric round-trip fixture. These are initial acceptance cases, not a replacement for the full asset, rig, animation, material, or cross-application objective. Unsupported source types must be reported explicitly; they must never silently produce a partially compatible asset.

Stage Required behavior Evidence required
Identity Explicit Blender and Unreal session IDs, source object identity, target project and asset path Native responses before preview; ambiguous sessions fail
Preview Describe source geometry, units, coordinate conversion, materials, destination, saves and placement Structured proposed changes; no source or destination mutation
Source protection Detect source changes after preview; preserve scene and exporter context Stale-preview rejection; selection, mode and scene comparison
Export Export through Blender's public API into private per-transfer staging Native export success, manifest, file checksum and size
Transfer validation Reject traversal, links, corrupt/changed files, excessive sizes and unsupported formats Rejection tests and repeat verification immediately before import
Import Use native Unreal editor APIs on the game thread; prevent unapproved overwrite Native import diagnostics; verified asset class and package location
Verify Measure imported geometry, unit conversion, orientation and material slots; inspect references Compare native measurements with declared export metadata; asymmetric geometry fixture
Placement Preview the target world and transform; place the verified asset with a native editor transaction Native actor/mesh identity, transform and world responses
Recovery Preserve recoverable backups; distinguish completed, rolled back, partial and unknown outcomes Fault injection at export, import, save and placement boundaries
Report Preserve token-free records of every stage and resulting asset paths Report with status, diagnostics, evidence and recovery actions
Acceptance Repeat on clean setup and in visible application sessions Install logs, regression results and interactive verification record

Existing destinations remain protected. Overwrite support requires a separate reviewable backup/restore workflow; the initial transfer contract rejects overwrites. No arbitrary script execution is required for the transfer workflow.

Full completion gates

  • Session handling: discover and explicitly select intended projects/scenes across multiple sessions; reject stale or changed identity at apply time.
  • Editing: verify native outcomes for scene/assets, Blueprint compiler results, materials, rigs, animation and evaluated Blender output. Document unsupported operations rather than inferring support from neighboring tools.
  • Recovery: exercise interrupted operations, stale previews, failed imports, overwrite protection, rollback failure and unknown outcomes. Keep records and recoverable material across process restarts.
  • Capability reporting: connect each supported workflow to native implementation, operation limits and its unit, subprocess, live and interactive acceptance evidence.
  • Installation: build reproducible packages for both adapters and verify clean installation, discovery, activation, connection and update behavior.

Current transfer implementation

server/core/transfer.py defines a versioned static-mesh manifest with source and target session identity, snapshot checksum, project/asset destination, geometry bounds/counts, source units, coordinate-system labels and material-slot metadata. It checks a staged artifact's filename, bounded size, binary FBX header, checksum, file identity and link/reparse restrictions. Integrity success explicitly does not claim valid FBX geometry, authorization, native export/import, or completed transfer.

Native Blender static-mesh export now exists in blender-addon/majestic_forge/exporting.py. Authenticated native export_preview / export_apply commands use expiring single-use previews, source fingerprints, private staging and persistent export status records. A disposable Blender test exports and reimports an asymmetric mesh, checking selection and active-object preservation, dimensions, material slots, stale/replay rejection and failed-export reports. Texture and group materials, animated or modified meshes are explicitly unsupported by this initial export stage.

Native Unreal staged static-mesh import now exists in ForgeMeshImport.cpp. The server stages verified artifacts into the explicit project's private Saved/ForgeTransfers/<transfer_id> directory, preserving a manifest and staging record. Native preview/apply revalidate identity and integrity, reject existing destinations and reused transfer records, hold a Windows read lease during import, and report saved geometry, material slots and bounded native warnings/errors.

An isolated UE 5.6 Editor build passed. A separate unattended Unreal process imported a factory Blender asymmetric mesh and verified signed vertices, units, bounds, counts, material slots, package save, wrong-session rejection, stale artifact/replay rejection and invalid-FBX rollback. For the current -Y-forward/Z-up FBX settings and forced Unreal X-front conversion, Blender (x, y, z) maps to Unreal (-y, -x, z) * meters_per_source_unit * 100 centimeters in this acceptance case. General object transforms and further unit settings require additional acceptance.

Native actor placement can now bind an exact loaded /Game/ static mesh through the existing unreal_preview_actors / unreal_apply_actors tools. Preview fingerprints the mesh instance, geometry/topology and material references as well as the target world/level and existing actors. Inspection reports the assigned mesh, material references and world bounds. A real MCP stdio acceptance run placed the imported fixture with nontrivial location, rotation and scale and verified these native results. The level remained unsaved; the test's own process was then closed.

Constant-PBR material transfer now supports opaque scene-linear base color, roughness, metallic and sidedness from an unlinked Principled shader. The exporter classifies unsupported graphs, transparency, advanced BSDF settings and animation. Material-transfer staging rejects unsupported or missing profiles before target writes. Native Unreal import creates new generated material packages, verifies their constant graphs, binds them to matching mesh slots and reports individual save results. The acceptance fixture verified native constants and the placed actor's material references. Shader compilation and visual equivalence remain explicitly unverified; this does not establish arbitrary Blender shader conversion.

Advanced material/texture transfer, cross-process recovery coordination, level saving, rendered-material verification and interactive transfer acceptance remain outstanding. Native import evidence does not establish final pipeline completion.

server/core/workflow_journal.py now provides private durable receipts with ordered export/staging/import/verification/placement stages, revision checks, atomic writes and operating-system file locks. Started native steps become uncertain on restart; the store never replays application operations. forge_inspect_transfer exposes read-only receipt inspection and explicitly distinguishes recorded state from currently verified application state. This is the coordinator's persistence foundation for the connected transfer coordinator.

server/core/workflows.py now connects native export, protected staging, import, geometry/material verification and actor placement through forge_preview_transfer and forge_apply_transfer. Explicit session IDs and adapter contract versions are required. Each native side effect receives a started receipt before execution; uncertain transport outcomes stop the workflow without automatic replay. Source and target identity are checked against the preview, existing destinations are rejected, and the source export remains available for recovery.

scripts/verify_transfer_workflow_mcp.py passed against separate factory Blender 5.2 and unattended Unreal 5.6 processes using real MCP stdio. The asymmetric mesh workflow completed all five stages, saved its mesh and material assets, verified native geometry and material graphs, placed an actor with nontrivial transform, preserved source scene facts and rejected replay. Evidence is retained under the disposable host's Saved/WorkflowAcceptance-* directories. This is headless native acceptance; the level remained unsaved and shader/rendered appearance and visible interactive use remain unverified. The current Python regression suite passes 121 tests, including coordinator boundary tests; Ruff passes for server and tests.

The same native MCP acceptance also passed with --variant transformed_metric: the source used an offset, nontrivial rotation, nonuniform object scale and a metric scene scale of 0.01 meters per unit. Complete imported signed vertex positions and bounds matched the declared world-space conversion. This verifies that additional fixture; it does not establish every transform or unit setting.

The acceptance runner now audits saved mesh/material package files and records their sizes/checksums, verifies the retained source FBX checksum, checks all five started/completed receipt pairs and compares the durable receipt with the MCP reply. --audit-existing <acceptance-directory> repeats these checks without starting application processes and reads the receipt through a fresh MCP server. This audit passed after the transformed fixture's native processes closed. The fresh server returned the same completed receipt with runtime verification and automatic native replay explicitly disabled. This establishes receipt persistence and retained files; reopening assets and native recovery reconciliation remain separate acceptance requirements.

scripts/verify_unreal_saved_transfer.py now verifies native asset reopening in a separate Unreal Python commandlet restricted to the generated disposable host. It passed for the transformed metric transfer: saved mesh/material assets loaded as their expected native classes, mesh material references matched the receipt, and opaque/sidedness settings survived saving. Package checksums were unchanged after the read-only probe. Evidence is retained under the acceptance directory's Reopen-* folder. This does not reopen a saved level, verify rendered appearance or complete native recovery reconciliation.

Native connected-workflow failure acceptance now rejects an existing destination without changing saved package checksums or target actors. It also previews a new transfer, edits the source transform through Blender MCP, and confirms stale-source rejection before staging/import with a failed durable receipt and no completed stages. This test exposed delayed Blender dependency-graph evaluation after scripted transforms; export snapshots now update the view layer before fingerprinting the world matrix. The corrected transformed-metric native acceptance passed. This does not establish interrupted-import or save-failure recovery.

Native save-failure acceptance now blocks a unique destination directory with an exclusive file in the disposable host. The first run exposed Unreal's fatal default save-error handling: the application disconnected and the coordinator correctly retained an unknown outcome. Mesh and material saves now use SAVE_NoError, allowing the importer to report package-write failures instead of terminating the editor. The isolated Editor target rebuilt successfully and the full native fixture passed: save failure returned partial, no assets were saved, placement was not attempted, and existing packages/actors remained unchanged. The fixture removes its own blocker and retains the source export and receipts. This verifies failure reporting and containment; recovery of the partial in-memory assets is not yet implemented or proven.

unreal_inspect_static_mesh now provides read-only native inspection of loaded meshes: bounded geometry, constant material graphs, package dirty flags and disk package presence. The updated isolated Editor build passed, as did all 121 Python tests and Ruff. A real MCP native save-failure fixture then verified that the partial mesh remained loaded with 8 vertices/12 triangles, its package was dirty, and neither it nor its generated material had a disk package. The server exposes 29 tools. This supplies current-state evidence for recovery decisions; it does not automatically save, discard, reimport or reconcile a retained operation.

forge_reconcile_transfer now connects a retained operation to explicit native session inspection. It rejects a different project before asset inspection and compares available loaded geometry/materials with recorded export metadata. A missing loaded mesh produces limited registry evidence without asserting disk absence. It never changes receipts or automatically replays operations. All 124 Python tests passed, including three reconciliation boundary tests. The native partial-import fixture passed through this MCP tool with geometry/materials verified and recovery explicitly incomplete. The server now exposes 30 tools.

One native acceptance attempt encountered receipt-storage failure after export; the coordinator retained the started receipt, returned unknown outcome and did not proceed to import. The retained source export was readable. A subsequent new disposable fixture passed. Receipt failures now include a bounded storage error code for diagnosis; the intermittent storage failure's cause remains unresolved.

The successful native transfer acceptance now modifies source vertex positions through actual blender_preview_scene / blender_apply_scene MCP calls before transfer. It verifies Blender reports preservation of the original mesh datablock, then compares the edited geometry's complete signed vertex positions after Unreal import. The transformed-metric run passed with this source-edit step plus asset saving, placement, overwrite/stale rejection, partial save reporting and read-only reconciliation. Source scene preservation is measured after the authorized edit; the transfer does not undo that edit or save the Blender scene.

The same successful MCP source-edit recipe now changes Principled base color to [0.12, 0.34, 0.56, 1], roughness to 0.27 and metallic to 0.63. Native transfer, save-failure and reconciliation acceptance passed with those non-default values. The saved-asset commandlet verifier now inspects the connected native Constant3Vector and Constant expressions after a fresh process loads the saved material. Their values matched the import receipt and package checksums remained unchanged. This proves saved constant graph values for this profile, not rendered equivalence or general shader conversion. Ruff and scoped whitespace checks passed for the updated verifiers.

The current source-only Blender ZIP passed expanded clean-profile installation acceptance on Blender 5.2.2. The verifier confirmed it imported the installed module from the isolated profile, registered the ForgeMCP panel, reported transfer contract version 1, rejected an incorrect token and caller-selected output path, performed native FBX export with matching size/checksum and complete small-mesh world-position metadata, preserved selection/active-object context, rejected replay and a scripted-transform stale preview, stopped/restarted the bridge and disabled cleanly. No preferences were saved and the user's profile/session was untouched. This is headless installed-package acceptance, not visual panel QA.

The current Unreal development ZIP is Artifacts/ForgeMCP-Unreal-Development-0.2.0-UE5.6.1-Win64.zip (23 files, SHA256 986be859518c51b03247932676e72687cd2a8902027fdda8edc5a529f5189948). Packaging checks current source/configuration against the isolated build, requires both editor/runtime modules, checks binary timestamps and the installed editor's BuildId, verifies ZIP contents and preserves replaced packages. Repeated packaging produced identical bytes. The final ZIP passed loading in a newly generated Blueprint-only project. Native health/project responses matched that project; process-module inspection confirmed its extracted DLL was loaded. The test closed only its own process and retained evidence in Saved/UnrealPackageAcceptance-*. This is Win64 development-package acceptance on the existing Unreal 5.6.1 machine, not a clean operating-system install or interactive release acceptance.

Visible panel acceptance remains unverified: the computer-use skill is installed, but its required node_repl runtime is not exposed in this agent session. No UI input or screenshot-based verification was performed.

Install-ForgeUnreal.ps1 now defaults to the current development ZIP instead of an older extracted artifact directory. Archive mode validates bounded size/count, manifest file scope, checksums, path traversal, Windows case aliases, encrypted entries and links before extraction writes. Extraction requires a new staging directory and refuses existing destinations. Running GUI and commandlet editors for the target project are checked before staging; existing plugin/project backups remain preserved. A fresh Blueprint-only project's native package acceptance now invokes the actual installer, confirms it enabled the plugin and then verifies the loaded DLL came from that installed project. That acceptance passed. All 131 Python tests and Ruff passed, including seven archive-boundary tests. Checksums establish archive integrity, not a publisher signature or trust in third-party code.

Coordinator receipt-failure regression now covers completion writes after export, staging, import and placement with both permission errors and journal-busy errors. Each case retains a started/uncertain receipt, reports only a bounded storage code, stops subsequent native operations, clears in-process active state and rejects preview replay. Additional tests confirm a failed started-receipt write prevents the corresponding export/import/placement request. These are protocol-fixture fault-injection tests with real receipt storage; they do not recreate or diagnose the earlier intermittent native storage failure.

Blender rig inspection now accepts optional include_evaluated. It reports native dependency-graph bone matrices in armature/world space and world-space head/tail positions at the current scene frame, bounded to 256 bones with finite-value checks. It does not change the frame. Default queries omit the new flag so older running adapters retain their existing inspection behavior.

Native recipe acceptance verified evaluated poses at two authored keyframe endpoints, different world matrices across those frames and expected world-space head positions under rig translation/nonuniform scale. Exact boolean validation also passed. Real MCP inspection and hierarchy/skin-weight/rig-creation acceptance passed in a separate factory session, with evidence under Saved/RigPoseAcceptance-f331ff36d9314516935ec94774dda067. All 142 Python tests and Ruff passed before the final compatibility adjustment; the final focused MCP regression also passed. The current Blender ZIP was rebuilt and passed isolated installation/export checks (SHA256 33bfc95548d84bbbc9dfc675818e328e35e03b9a44cd0fd82c9695faccd588af). This establishes bounded current-frame evaluated inspection and the tested native animation fixture; visible playback, broader rig workflows and animation transfer remain separate completion requirements.

Recovery-journal reads now replay the bounded event sequence to derive state, active stage and completed stages, then compare those values with the receipt's reported summary. Completion without events, completion without a start, skipped stages, duplicate starts and events after terminal outcomes are rejected. All 147 Python tests and Ruff passed. A fresh MCP server also read the retained native material-transfer receipt successfully through the persistence audit, confirming valid existing records remain compatible. This enforces receipt consistency; it does not authenticate event claims or replace native reconciliation.

Retained-export recovery is now connected through forge_preview_asset_recovery and forge_apply_asset_recovery (32 MCP tools total). Eligible incomplete transfers with completed export/staging evidence can restore to an absent new destination in the same project. Preview checks artifact integrity and binds target session, project/level and original receipt revision. Apply consumes the preview once and creates a separate recovery receipt with staging/import/verification stages. It performs no new Blender export, preserves partial assets and original receipts, and verifies/saves the new mesh/material assets without actor placement or level saving. Failure or uncertainty stops without replay.

Native transformed-metric acceptance passed with Blender closed before recovery. The save-failure fixture's retained FBX restored into a new destination; native geometry/material reconciliation passed, original receipt and existing actors/ packages remained unchanged, and recovery replay was rejected. Evidence is in Saved/TransferImportValidation-f81c125453ba42a7871d9b9f8f9176fe/HostProject/Saved/WorkflowAcceptance-6ee6758fa98c40faa6eecc0928219d36. This verifies the new-destination restoration path; saving/discarding the original partial in-memory assets and automatic placement recovery remain unfinished.

All 154 Python tests and Ruff passed, including recovery cases for absent Blender, unchanged original receipts, replay/confirmation, stale context, wrong project, active originals and changed retained artifacts. The saved-asset verifier's new --recovery mode also passed in a fresh Unreal commandlet: restored mesh/materials loaded, references and constant graph values matched, and package checksums remained unchanged. Original partial objects and actor/level recovery are still separate work.

Blender add-on 0.2.1 fixes an installation/update failure reported in Blender 5.2: the new exporter could encounter an older cached materials module without transfer_surface even though the replacement file on disk contained it. Package initialization now reloads cached helpers in dependency order before importing their symbols. The isolated installed-ZIP test reproduces the missing cached function, re-enables the add-on and verifies panel registration, bridge startup and export preview. Clean installation, native authenticated export, stale/replay rejection and disable cleanup passed against Blender 5.2.2. The corrected ZIP is Artifacts/ForgeMCP-Blender-Addon-0.2.1.zip; the existing user session was untouched.

Recovery can now use the retained export of an eligible incomplete recovery, with completed staging required and the retained transfer ID bound to that receipt's operation ID. A fresh preview and a different absent destination are required; neither earlier receipt is modified and no native operation is replayed. Protocol regression verifies recovery after a server restart and rejects a changed artifact belonging to the interrupted recovery. All 156 Python tests passed.

Native transformed-metric MCP acceptance now deliberately blocks saves during a first recovery, verifies its partial result and restores from that recovery's retained FBX into a second new destination with Blender closed. The original transfer and failed-recovery receipts, existing package checksums and actors remain unchanged. The restored mesh/material reopened in a fresh Unreal commandlet with matching references and constant graphs and unchanged package checksums. A fresh MCP server separately inspected all three receipts and verified their staged-FBX checksums and recorded lineage after the native processes closed. Evidence is in Saved/TransferImportValidation-f81c125453ba42a7871d9b9f8f9176fe/HostProject/Saved/WorkflowAcceptance-fc3c0ee8aa9f4129aa72129f50b5a0db. Ruff passed. This validates native save-failure recovery chaining and persistent evidence; it does not establish recovery from every interruption, visible UI use, shader appearance or saved-level/actor reopening. Those gates remain open.

scripts/verify_unreal_level_persistence.py now establishes the native API foundation for reviewed level saving. In the generated disposable host, a first Unreal commandlet creates a new blank map, loads the recovered mesh/material and places an actor with nontrivial transform, then saves to a unique absent map path. A second commandlet loads that saved map and verifies actor identity by unique label, world package identity, transform and mesh/material references. The saved map checksum remains unchanged during reopening; existing asset checksums remain unchanged through both stages. Evidence is under the latest workflow acceptance's LevelPersistence-c712b994cd164fda9c5efe84a6e5d830 directory. Ruff passed. This fixture calls native Unreal Python APIs directly and creates its own actor; it does not prove persistence of the original MCP-placed actor or implement a reviewed MCP level-save operation. The next implementation must bind a save preview to the selected editor world and its state, protect existing map destinations, report failed/uncertain saves and verify the MCP-placed actor after reopening. Streaming/world-partition behavior, interactive acceptance and rendered appearance also remain open. The complete development goal remains unfinished.

Reviewed native level saving is now connected through unreal_preview_level_save / unreal_apply_level_save (34 MCP tools). Preview binds bounded nontransient world-package state and map identity; apply requires matching confirmation, a fresh destination folder and unchanged state. Win64 destination checks reject reserved names/reparse ancestors. Existing map folders are protected. Saving may change current world package identity and does not save referenced mesh/material assets. Native intent/result records are retained under Saved/ForgeLevelSaves; partial or uncertain results never claim rollback/reopen.

The isolated Unreal Editor build passed. Real transformed-metric MCP acceptance saved the original MCP-placed actor to a new map. Actor edits after preview caused stale rejection before destination creation; consumed-preview replay and an existing destination were rejected. The saved map reopened in a fresh Unreal commandlet: original actor object name/label, transform and mesh/material references matched. Read-only reopening preserved map and asset checksums. Evidence is in WorkflowAcceptance-b4de8b0487824770a1e6d0f5c546517d, with reopening evidence under LevelPersistence-0b9fc8ea9b61440aa0ca744ce33480df. All 156 Python tests and Ruff passed. The Unreal development ZIP was rebuilt from matching source/binaries (SHA256 cdf4638f64192b880c6838874252152beb2932ea58d0751ea2d7658b7fdfced6). The actual archive installer and extracted DLL load passed in a fresh Blueprint-only project under Saved/UnrealPackageAcceptance-e10db7abf38a487a851c4d8ef208b739. Its retained native health response includes both level-save commands. Existing user-session binaries were not replaced; this is isolated package acceptance. Native records still need the server store's crash-durability/reconciliation guarantees, map-save failure acceptance and reviewed handling of unsaved referenced assets. World-partition/streaming support, visible interactive use and rendered appearance remain unfinished requirements of the full goal.

server/core/levels.py now wraps level saves with the same private, fsynced, OS-locked receipt store used for transfers. Preview binds explicit session token identity and target project/world. Apply requires matching confirmation, consumes the preview once, writes a level_save started event before the native request and records completed/partial/unknown results separately from transport success. An intent-write failure prevents native saving; a completion-write failure retains uncertainty. Restart inspection never replays. Native uppercase GUIDs are retained for bridge calls while public receipt IDs are normalized to lowercase; the native operation ID is also retained in the plan for uncertain-result correlation.

All 164 Python tests passed. New protocol fault tests cover timeout/disconnection, malformed native responses, started/completion receipt-write failures, wrong session/confirmation, changed session binding and native GUID casing. Final focused level/receipt regression passed after the metadata addition; Ruff passed. Native transformed-metric MCP acceptance saved and inspected the level receipt, rejected stale/replayed saves, and passed the complete transfer/recovery sequence. A fault injected immediately after a second layer was created caused a clean rollback; the apply result had no rollback errors and an MCP inspection confirmed that the failed layer was absent. Evidence is retained at Saved/TransferImportValidation-f81c125453ba42a7871d9b9f8f9176fe/HostProject/Saved/WorkflowAcceptance-a94a2f5d780c4f3ba4b4941b3bdb96d8/acceptance.json.

Blender 5.2.2 clean-profile package 0.2.24 passed installation, UV layer create/edit/read-back, lifecycle and export acceptance. All 277 Python tests and Ruff passed. This closes UV-layer initialization for bounded static mesh work; unwrap/seam tools and broader recovery, sidecar, material/texture, skeletal/animation transfer and real-time synchronization remain outstanding.

Reviewed Blender Smart UV Project — 2026-10-11

Added a typed smart_uv_project scene operation backed by Blender's native Smart UV Project operator. It accepts one exact layer name, a 0-to-90-degree angle limit and a bounded island margin; it creates the target layer when missing and is limited to 200,000 loops. The bridge temporarily manages selection and Edit Mode, validates the resulting coordinates, and restores the previous selection and mode. Preview fingerprints include topology, target layer names and all UV values on the layer. Mutations use the copied-mesh rollback transaction.

Actual native MCP stdio acceptance projected and read back six loop UVs, rejected a competing preview after the mesh changed, injected failure after projection, and verified exact UV restoration with zero rollback errors. Evidence: Saved/TransferImportValidation-f81c125453ba42a7871d9b9f8f9176fe/HostProject/Saved/WorkflowAcceptance-e130c52eb760434dac3c4fc90c53599e/acceptance.json. Blender 5.2.2 clean-profile package 0.2.25 passed create/edit/project/read-back, lifecycle and export checks. All 278 Python tests and Ruff passed. Seam tools and packing optimization remain open, along with replacement recovery, sidecars, material/texture and skeletal/animation transfer, and real-time synchronization.

Reviewed Blender mesh seam inspection/editing — 2026-10-11

Added native mesh_edge_info and MCP tool blender_inspect_mesh_edges for bounded pages of edge indices, endpoints, seam flags and sharp flags. The typed set_mesh_edge_seams scene operation changes up to 512 unique edge flags in a reviewed recipe. Preview fingerprints include the requested edge seam values; apply copies the mesh datablock, writes and verifies the changes, and uses the existing rollback path on failure.

The real MCP stdio run on disposable Blender 5.2.2 inspected five edges, applied a seam, rejected a stale competing preview, injected a post-write failure and verified the seam stayed at its original value after rollback, with zero rollback errors. Evidence: Saved/TransferImportValidation-f81c125453ba42a7871d9b9f8f9176fe/HostProject/Saved/WorkflowAcceptance-3dff767e4bf442b19f41ae0056c5cbe9/acceptance.json. Clean-profile Blender package 0.2.26 passed seam and UV operations plus lifecycle and export checks. All 279 Python tests and Ruff passed. Sharp-flag editing, seam-aware unwrap/packing, broader transfer payloads and live sync remain open.

Reviewed Blender seam-aware UV unwrap — 2026-10-11

Added the unwrap_uv scene operation for Blender's native ANGLE_BASED and CONFORMAL unwrap methods. It requires at least one seam edge, accepts a bounded UV margin, can create the named UV layer if needed and is limited to 200,000 loops. The helper activates the requested layer, switches selection and Edit Mode safely, verifies finite normalized coordinates and restores prior editor selection/mode. Preview fingerprints include every target UV coordinate and the mesh's full seam map; apply edits a copied mesh for rollback.

Actual MCP stdio acceptance marked all 12 edges on the disposable factory Cube, unwrapped and inspected all 24 loop UVs, rejected a stale competing preview, then injected a failure after unwrap and verified exact restoration with zero rollback errors. Evidence: Saved/TransferImportValidation-f81c125453ba42a7871d9b9f8f9176fe/HostProject/Saved/WorkflowAcceptance-07ee4d942c9544b5be9ffc2989bb6ac4/acceptance.json. Blender 5.2.2 package 0.2.27 passed clean-profile seam/unwrap and lifecycle/export checks. All 280 tests and Ruff passed. Automated seam placement, UV packing, remaining transfer payloads and real-time synchronization remain outstanding.

Reviewed Blender UV island packing — 2026-10-11

Added the typed pack_uv_islands recipe for Blender's native island packer. It requires an existing named UV layer, local mesh in Object Mode, a margin from 0 to 0.5, and no more than 200,000 loops. Preview fingerprints bind topology and the target layer's current UV values; apply uses a copied mesh, validates normalized output and restores selection/active object. Actual MCP stdio acceptance packed and read back all 24 UV loops, rejected stale previews, and verified exact rollback after an injected post-pack failure. The Blender 5.2.2 clean-profile 0.2.28 ZIP passed UV, export, install and lifecycle checks. All 281 Python tests and Ruff passed. Evidence and package hash are recorded in Development_Status.md. Remaining priorities include seam placement, richer mesh/material/texture/skeletal/animation transfer, and eventual live sync.

Reviewed Unreal actor search — 2026-10-11

Added read-only unreal_find_actors for bounded active-world search by case-insensitive name/label substring, exact class path and exact actor tag, with combined filters, pagination and optional transform output. Server/plugin version 0.2.1 passed UE 5.6.1 compile/link, clean package load, MCP stdio result verification, and missing-filter rejection. The current Blender 0.2.29 package also passed its clean-profile verifier; no Blender version bump was needed for this Unreal-only change. The reference catalog now records both actor-search registrations as partial rather than missing. Exact tag search and optional transforms are implemented; property predicates and exact/wildcard name patterns remain open. See Development_Status.md for native MCP acceptance evidence. The connected editor still requires the updated plugin and reconnect to expose this increment in its live tool registry.

Reviewed Blender existing Action key editing

blender_inspect_animation provides bounded, paged inspection of active Action F-curves and keys. The reviewed set_keyframe recipe edits one inspected curve and key index, with bounded frame/value data, collision rejection, stale-scene fingerprinting, a copied Action and native read-back. The Blender add-on advanced to 0.2.30. Clean-profile ZIP and disposable MCP acceptance passed; see Development_Status.md for evidence and package hash. Key deletion, interpolation and handle editing, NLA, retargeting and animation transfer remain separate work. The live Blender add-on is still 0.2.3 and does not expose this increment yet.

For the cross-application workflow, the roadmap's user-facing handoff labels are Send to Unreal in Blender and Send to Blender / Import from Blender in Unreal. These are staged transfer operations today. Keep real-time synchronization as a later milestone requiring revision detection, two-sided conflict resolution, loop suppression, recovery and an explicit enable/disable control; do not describe the current transfer tools as live synchronization.

Unreal Content Browser and session discovery — server 0.2.4 / plugin 0.2.3

The Unreal 0.2.3 plugin and server 0.2.4 expose bounded Content Browser selection inspection, native opening of one exact project/plugin asset, and Content Browser synchronization. These are UI-level navigation operations with no asset edit/save behavior. The plugin build, clean package load, stdio tool registration, and disposable cross-application MCP acceptance passed. A headless native run returned a valid empty selection and accepted the sync request; visible navigation could not be verified. Server 0.2.4 checks the 64 most recent regular registration files after testing exposed alphabetical truncation hiding a new Editor session behind stale registrations. A regression test covers this case. Asset opening explicitly rejects unattended hosts; the interactive editor path still needs verification after an Editor session reconnects. Keep Blender add-on version 0.2.30 unchanged until a validated Blender-specific change lands.

Live connector checkpoint: Codex currently reports ForgeMCP server 0.2.0 and zero connected sessions. Restart/reconnect ForgeMCP and relaunch the intended Unreal and Blender applications to activate and verify these source/package increments.

Current development continuation — DataAsset editing and Blender graph completion

Unreal's DataAsset class/instance discovery and native class property-schema inspection now cover a broader read-only slice of the audited DataAsset module. The next Unreal increment should extend reviewed edits to existing DataAsset instances, with stale-state checks, atomic rollback, explicit save and reopen verification, then widen existing material graph editing. Do not treat generic asset scalar edits as full DataAsset authoring.

For Blender, the first existing-graph edit slice now adds allowlisted nodes and links onto unoccupied inputs; it verifies endpoint types and cycles, fingerprints the inspected graph for stale-preview rejection, reads native results back and removes added nodes/links on rollback. Existing-node edits now support bounded positions, selected Math/VectorMath operations, MixRGB blend modes and supported unlinked scalar/vector/color defaults, with stale-preview and rollback checks. Existing-node/link removal/replacement and broader node coverage remain open. Continue filling animation/NLA, rig controls, texture transfer and two-sided synchronization afterward. Advance component versions only with native acceptance and clean package verification; v1.0 remains gated on the full roadmap and interactive activation.

Current release checkpoint: Unreal plugin 0.2.8, MCP server 0.3.1, Blender add-on 0.2.32. Guarded DataAsset creation and reviewed Blender existing-node graph edits passed disposable native acceptance. Both packages passed fresh-project/profile load checks; the broader Unreal host Editor target build remains unresolved. Next, extend existing DataAsset instance editing and Blender graph node/link management, then broaden session activation and recovery acceptance before v1.0.0.
